children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a positive start on November 25, tracking GIFT Nifty, which is trading higher at 25,739 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol

Indian equity benchmarks snapped their two-day winning streak and ended lower on November 23, with the Nifty falling 1.7 percent, marking its biggest single-day decline in nearly five months. Broad-based selling in auto, metal and financial stocks dragged the benchmarks lower.
At close, the Sensex was down 1,483.72 points or 1.77 percent at 82,435.99, and the Nifty was down 450.95 points or 1.75 percent at 25,349.65.
Biggest Nifty lowers were Tata Steel, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, Hindalco, HDFC Bank, while gainers included TCS, Tech Mahindra, Shriram Finance, HCL Technologies, Titan Company.
On the sectoral front, except Information Technology and Consumer Durables, all other sectoral indices ended in the red Metal, Oil & Gas, PSU Bank, Private Bank, Infra, Energy, Auto down 1-3 percent.
The broader markets outperformed the benchmark indices, with the Nifty Midcap index falling 0.7 percent, while the Nifty Smallcap index losing 0.66%.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Up)
GIFT Nifty was trading higher at around 25,739 in early trade, indicating a positive start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Down)

Asian stocks retreated after a selloff in US technology shares revived doubts about the durability of the artificial intelligence trade, extending losses from Wall Street into the region. Treasuries held gains as haven demand persisted.
The MSCI Asia Pacific Index slipped 1%, losing ground after posting its biggest rally since July on Tuesday. The losses were led by South Korea’s Kospi index, which declined 4.8%.
US Equities (Mixed)
The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 closed lower on Tuesday as ​Nvidia and other AI-related shares gave back some of the previous day's sharp gains and investors braced for possible new tariffs.

The Dow Jones ​Industrial Average rose 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70, the S&P 500 lost 36.08 points, or 0.50%, to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 356.02 ​points, or 1.48%, to 23,733.54.
Dollar Index (Up)

The US dollar took a breather on Wednesday ahead of inflation and growth data, the last major readings before a December Federal Reserve policy meeting at which traders see a 97% chance of an interest rate hike.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against six peers, was flat at 103.85 following a 0.44% slide in the prior session. The euro was down 0.03% at $1.0961.
US Bond Yield (Down)
The yield on 10-year Treasuries and 2-year Treasury bonds down more than 1 basis point each at 4.91% and 4.67%, respectively.
Asian currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies traded on a mixed note against the US dollar, with the Indonesian rupiah, South Korean won, Japanese yen, Thai baht and Taiwan dollar registering losses. The Taiwan dollar was the worst performer, declining 0.249 percent, followed by the Indonesian rupiah, which slipped 0.148 percent, and the South Korean won, which eased 0.113 percent. The Japanese yen and Thai baht edged lower by 0.019 percent and 0.021 percent, respectively.

On the other hand, the Philippine peso gained 0.165 percent, emerging as the best-performing Asian currency, while the Malaysian ringgit advanced 0.134 percent. The Chinese renminbi and Singapore dollar also posted marginal gains of 0.044 percent and 0.008 percent, respectively.
Crude (Slips)
Oil steadied as traders weighed signs of rising supply against escalating attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent traded around $91 a barrel after advancing 2.3% in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate was below $82.
Gold (Down)

Gold prices edged lower on Wednesday after falling more than 2% in the previous session, as hawkish signals from the US Federal Reserve reinforced expectations of a December rate hike, while investors awaited US inflation data for further policy clues.
Spot gold fell 0.3% to $3,544.54 per ounce, while US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.5% to $3,542.60.
Fund Flow Action

On November 23, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) remained net sellers for the fourth consecutive session, offloading equities worth Rs 2,760 crore. Meanwhile, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) continued their buying streak for the tenth consecutive session, purchasing equities worth Rs 5,672 crore.
